svg.text: R2 + C without supports: a route worth testing
A geometric feasibility study, not a printable redesign.
Keep rounded shoulders, broaden the flat panels, and assemble the hinge after printing.
Earlier R2: small flat patch under an oval
R2-S study: flatter faces + curved shoulders
Flat patch ≈31 mm across; first widening is steep.
Rounding the underside alone does not remove support needs.
Flat landing ≈100 mm; max 0.16 mm growth per 0.20 mm layer.
Trial shell ≈264 ×132 ×60 mm. Broader flats are the tradeoff.
C HINGE • A SAMPLED OPENING ROUTE
Both joints move together. A 44 mm link spacing and 0.6 mm nominal rim gap pass this section screen.
Bodies, contents, separator and table were checked. Green links, bearing mounts and covers were NOT checked as solids.

svg.text: PRINT STRATEGY • SEPARATE PARTS, ONE MATERIAL
Two open shell halves
Exterior flat panels on the bed; mouths upward.
Shallow end ramps must finish below the long brush.
Rear slots need covered clearance when shut.
Two flat links + four printed pins
Print link plates flat; their eye holes face upward.
Print short pins upright; retain them positively.
No TPU or purchased hinge hardware assumed.
Bearing blocks and the remaining checks
Use open / sloping roofs at horizontal pin holes.
Mounts must grow from floors or sloping buttresses.
Still needs full 3D CAD and Orca support probing.
What this establishes: a plausible shell-growth rule and a connected, manually guided section opening path.
What remains unknown: covered hinge slots, link / mount interference, 3D corners, clip placement, print behavior and easy operation.
The smaller 14 mm link tried in this same layout collides in the flat-open pose. A tiny hidden link is not a finished C mechanism.
Study: 1,891 coarse poses; selected route refined to 0.2° steps. No production CAD, exports or print-status records changed.
